title: Grok Bot adds its own email addresses on a grokbot.com mail domain
why: Summary: bots can now claim an inbox and contact businesses themselves; any city use stays behind the Council and the owner's no-send-unasked rule.

title: Leaked XPass tiers would bundle X Premium, SuperGrok, Cursor and Grok Bot in one shared usage pool
source: X News (summary of posts, unconfirmed leak)
why: Summary: if real, Grok Build and Grok Bot quotas could merge, which would change how the Treasury paces both pools. Watch for an official announcement before acting.

title: PersonalAgentBench scores agents on real-account tasks for completion and trust
why: Summary: a trust-plus-completion benchmark is a useful yardstick for the city's own agents; the Critic can borrow its two-axis scoring.

title: Release workflow run end to end by coordinated Grok Bots in Slack
why: Summary: a release bot delegating builds, fuzz swarms and fixes to an engineer bot mirrors the city's Grok Bot to Grok Build Channel handoff, with humans approving only the final step.

title: Grok 4.7 tops VulcanBench coding and the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index
why: Summary: Grok 4.7 stays the strongest main lane for hard Grok Build tasks, so free OmniRoute lanes should take routine work and Main Grok only the hard turns.

title: Grok Build 1.0.50: worktree rm refuses dirty or in-use worktrees without -f
why: A remove that stops when a worktree is dirty or in use keeps the city from deleting the owner's work by mistake.

title: Grok Build 1.0.46: session-start rules survive prompt rebuilds; grok inspect reports MCP sources
why: The city's global rule and SessionStart hook load at session start; this fix keeps them in force in long sessions. Worth being on 1.0.46+ (grok update).

title: Grok Build 1.0.44 adds /context-window and per-model context choices
why: A smaller context window for routine sessions (city-apply, quick fixes) is a direct token saving; keep the big window for refactors.

title: "Time to rewrite" (TTR): measuring how agent-ready a codebase is
why: Same idea as AGENTS.md: specs next to code and tests an agent can run. Supports keeping the city's AGENTS.md and tests current every session.

title: Temperature 0 does not make LLM output repeatable (batch size, kernels, float math)
source: Thinking Machines Lab; X discussion Oct 7
why: Agent checks must test outcomes (files, exit codes), never exact model wording; the city-apply checks and tests already follow this.

title: Reflection AI announces Beam: 501B open-weight MoE (23B active) for coding and agents
why: Reported 80.9 on SWE-bench with Apache-2.0 weights promised later this month; a candidate for the Scout to check once the weights are actually out.

title: Grok 4.7 reported at the top of VulcanBench coding and the AA Cyber Index
why: Grok Build and Grok Bot run on it: no model switch needed for coding work; the Council keeps the strongest tier for King verdicts only.

title: OpenAI posts AI-found math results with Lean-checked proofs
why: Shows how proofs get machine-checked; a good motivation for the Tutor's Calc I rigor problems (epsilon-delta, derivative rules). Claims still under review by mathematicians.

title: Cogent Security launches Attack Path Analysis for AI agent swarm risks
why: Agent-swarm attack-path tooling underscores why R-006 lethal-trifecta hardening is top priority before more city autonomy.
